headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 1.13 (95% CI: 0.98–1.3), indicating no statistically significant association between sugar-sweetened beverage intake and kidney and renal pelvis cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 75.14%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
